key_insight: Geometric nonlinearity alone creates a distinct near-crack-tip nonlinear zone in soft elastic solids, with a physical length scale that grows quadratically with the stress intensity factor.
engineering_relevance: This provides a clean baseline for predicting fracture in highly deformable solids and for separating geometry-driven effects from true material toughening.
method: Modelled a compressible St. Venant-Kirchhoff solid to isolate geometric nonlinearity from material nonlinearity.
Analyzed mode I plane-strain cracks using CTOD-based postprocessing and asymptotic analysis.
Used matched asymptotics to define the nonlinear length scale λ_nl and its scaling with K_I.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical asymptotic solutions and a CTOD-based near-tip comparison showing a departure from linear elastic predictions, but no experimental dataset is mentioned.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on an idealized constitutive model and plane-strain mode I setting, so transfer to real soft materials with strong material nonlinearity may require additional validation.
paper_title: Crack-Tip Opening as a Probe for Length-Scale Separation in Geometrically Nonlinear Solids
